# Rediscovered state publication fixtures

Verified September 5, 2026 using ordinary anonymous official HTTPS reads. This new module improves the failed sources without reading the original application's database. Captures omit site contacts and unrelated markup. No reporting form was opened or submitted.

## Iowa

The [official hub](https://www.iowaattorneygeneral.gov/for-consumers/security-breach-notifications/) publishes its annual URLs in a `breachYears` JavaScript array, rather than static select options. The [2026 archive](https://www.iowaattorneygeneral.gov/for-consumers/security-breach-notifications/2026-security-breach-notification) and [2025 archive](https://www.iowaattorneygeneral.gov/for-consumers/security-breach-notifications/2025-security-breach-notification) returned HTTP 200 through an ordinary identifiable request. They contain 29 and 68 reports respectively; 2025 includes a separately linked related entity and a supplemental-only notice. Both pages describe the dates as reported dates; the hub explains notices are ordered by receipt from the business.

- `rediscovered_states_iowa_navigation.html`: the actual published 2011–2026 navigation data, with unrelated JavaScript removed. URLs are discovered, never generated by evaluating JavaScript or guessing a year pattern.
- `rediscovered_states_iowa2026.html`: actual first card plus the last three cards, preserving their nested structure caused by missing closing article tags. The literal `0 notices listed` placeholder does not establish an empty result.
- `rediscovered_states_iowa2025.html`: selected actual cards preserving hidden `data-related-breaches="none"` placeholders, the separate Lewis Central Community School District entry, supplemental links, and the supplemental-only Landmark entry. Placeholder entities are excluded, actual related entities included.

The hub's generated JavaScript navigation is stale for several historical years. The linked [official sitemap](https://www.iowaattorneygeneral.gov/sitemap) supplies the actual plural URLs for 2022, 2021, 2018, 2016–2011 and bare-year paths for 2019 and 2017. Discovery prefers those published sitemap links, rather than guessing replacements or stopping at the stale links' HTTP 404 responses. After the shared client was updated to the accurate project identity, bounded collection reached all 16 annual archives, 2011–2026. The default annual-page budget is 16; explicit smaller budgets remain partial and report the exact collected years.

- `rediscovered_states_iowa_sitemap.html`: all 16 actual annual links from the official sitemap.
- `rediscovered_states_iowa2024_links.html`: actual broken initial `href="="` (one rejected row), a nested grid wrapper, and an external informational link beside a valid official notice PDF. The optional external page is not fetched. Structural wrappers do not create duplicate reports.

Full archive collection retains 677 reports from 688 actual rows. One broken initial link and ten rows with ambiguous identities from reused document URLs are withheld. This is partial data quality across all published annual pages, rather than a two-year collection window. PDF contents and supplemental documents remain outside routine collection. GitHub-runner access is separately checked by the parent task.

## Maine

The [current page](https://www.maine.gov/ag/consumer-protection/data-security-breaches) links its [public Archives](https://www.maine.gov/ag/news-and-library/archives), which still publish two redacted Excel files:

- [December 6, 2018 through September 14, 2020](https://www.maine.gov/ag/sites/maine.gov.ag/files/docs/Data%20breach%20spreadsheet%2012-6-2018%20through%209-14-2020%20REDACTED.xlsx)
- [August 1, 2010 through December 5, 2018](https://www.maine.gov/ag/sites/maine.gov.ag/files/docs/Data%20breach%20spreadsheet%208-1-2021%20through%2012-5-2018%20REDACTED.xlsx) — the source filename says `2021`; the published link label and report contents establish the historical period, so the collector does not infer coverage from that filename.

Both downloads returned HTTP 200 (239,392 and 1,026,018 bytes). The newer archive contains 985 report rows. The older contains 2,070 report rows: 60 ambiguous combined organization/address fields are withheld, and four rows sharing two conflicting derived identities are also withheld. The combined live parser produced 2,991 normalized reports and 64 explicit rejections from 3,055 rows. Neither current health nor current breach dates are inferred from retrieval time.

- `rediscovered_states_maine_archives.html`: the two exact published links and their source labels.
- `rediscovered_states_maine_submission_cells.json`: actual header and first two rows, restricted to organization, completion/breach dates, affected counts, and data-type fields. Addresses and reporter/service-contact fields are omitted.
- `rediscovered_states_maine_legacy_cells.json`: actual header/date/count layout; two organization cells are replaced with explicitly synthetic names/address text to exercise safe extraction. Not evidence about those synthetic organizations.

Tests construct tiny OOXML workbooks from these cell fixtures. They exercise shared-string, numeric and native boolean cells; huge formatting dimensions without allocating the rectangle; compressed and expanded byte limits, actual row and cell budgets; formula/error/schema and UTF-16 declaration rejection; date-system checks; date/count uncertainty; stable derived identities; and conflict accounting. Limits are 20 MB compressed, 40 MB expanded, 100 members, 20,000 actual rows including blank rows, and 1,000,000 actual cells. Encrypted or nonstandard compressed members are rejected. Native boolean cells cannot become affected counts or Excel serial dates. The full downloaded workbooks were also parsed outside Git.

Maine did not withdraw every historical publication. Its [June 12, 2026 official statement](https://www.maine.gov/ag/news-and-library/press-releases/statement-office-maine-attorney-general-abuse-data-breach-reporting) explains the current database withdrawal after false reports. Current navigation to `/ag/news-and-library/data-breach-notices` redirects to that offline-status page; a search-indexed 2026 detail at the former `/agviewer/content/ag/...` endpoint returned HTTP 403. The library offers a reporting form, not a replacement current export. Recovery is therefore explicitly historical, through September 2020. A restored current-page status fails for rediscovery rather than continuing to claim the database is offline.

## North Dakota discovery boundary

No replacement adapter is claimed. Discovery covered current Consumer Protection navigation; official search-engine results; the advertised public WordPress REST routes; public post/page searches for `breach`, `security`, and `notification`; public media searches for `breach` and one previously indexed notice filename; and first pages of public 2021/2025/2026 media results. The breach search returned only the [Identity Theft](https://attorneygeneral.nd.gov/consumer-resources/identity-theft/) and [Preventing Identity Theft](https://attorneygeneral.nd.gov/consumer-resources/identity-theft/preventing-identity-theft/) guidance pages, neither a filing register. Public media search returned no breach-labelled records. The ordinary site search returned HTTP 500.

The old directory and the search-indexed [2021 Thrifty Drug notice](https://attorneygeneral.nd.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/2021-04-28-ThriftyDrug.pdf) both returned HTTP 404. Search-index presence is not current document availability. The site's robots file also advertises [its sitemap index](https://attorneygeneral.nd.gov/sitemap_index.xml); its published page/post sitemaps were checked for a new public filing path. This evidence does not establish that no such publication can exist anywhere, only that no current official reusable source was verified in these discovery surfaces. No generic agency document, news report, or inaccessible historical PDF is substituted as a new filing.
